decisions.reason: Despite the public launch, this generic address autocomplete service sits only loosely within the firm's regulated-energy platform direction and the lack of later visibility makes it easier for management to stop backing it and redirect effort to more core offerings.

This Austrian gas grid fee database is close to the firm's core data business and platform strategy, so prior investment, public commitment, and the ability to blame weak uptake on market-entry timing would push management to persist with it.

The peak load window determination service fits the firm's analytical and compliance-focused offer, making it strategically central enough that management would be inclined to continue it rather than admit the launch was premature.

An end-customer tariff database builds directly on the firm's long-developed data assets and supports its broader digital-platform narrative, which under escalation-of-commitment logic favors continued support.

Custom web services are less aligned with the stated move toward standardized SaaS and modular products, and because they rely more on ongoing delivery than on a distinctive sunk product asset, management has less reason to keep this specific launch alive.

The postal code lookup service is a relatively generic add-on with limited strategic importance to the firm's regulated-energy specialization, so even with some launch commitment it is the kind of peripheral product management would let go.
